name: Overlook at Thornton
headline: Overlook at Thornton is an existing 160-unit, 1973-built apartment complex at 647 W. 91st Avenue in Thornton, long run by Adams County's housing authority (now Maiker Housing Partners), being acquired and rehabilitated as a 60% AMI tax credit property by 647 OAT, LLLP; it won $3,425,457 a year in 2022 federal 4% credit and $43.5M of bonds issued by the housing authority itself.
why_it_matters: It is a housing authority recapitalizing its own aging portfolio with self-issued bonds and 4% credit, keeping all 160 homes at or below 60% AMI.

status.label: Bonds issued October 2023; rehab completion not confirmed; 8609s not yet issued
status.detail: Bond counsel announced the $43.5M Series 2023 bonds on 2023-10-30 and said the work was expected to take 19 months, which would have put completion around mid-2025 (inferred). No dated permit, completion or placed-in-service record was found, and CHFA still lists the deal on its 2026-09-21 award report, which excludes developments with 8609s issued.

next_step: Look for Thornton building permit or final inspection records for 647/773 W. 91st Ave and for 8609 issuance.

key_numbers.meaning: 60 one-bedrooms, 75 two-bedrooms and 25 three-bedrooms; rents capped at 30% of 60% AMI.
About $34.3M over 10 years (inferred); no state credit shown.
Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds (Overlook at Thornton Project) Series 2023, issued by Maiker (legally the Adams County Housing Authority).

background.text: The property was already an Adams County Housing Authority (ACHA) affordable property before this deal: a 2009 post by the architects describes a full interior and exterior remodel after 2006 as-built drawings, and an ACHA news item describes a Colorado Health Foundation grant of $46,500 for a new playground for Overlook children.

The 2022 deal is a recapitalization: bond proceeds finance acquisition by 647 OAT, LLLP plus rehabilitation; the seller was presumably the housing authority itself, but no sale price appears in the county's public sales table (inferred).
All 160 units are to be held for households at or below 60% AMI with rents capped at 30% of 60% AMI, per the bond documents summary.
The deal does not appear in CHFA's 2022 Round One or Round Two competitive application narratives; it was a rolling 4% bond deal only.

CHFA's 4% award report says it leaves out developments whose IRS Form 8609s have been issued; this deal is still listed on the 2026-09-21 report, so 8609s had not been issued by then (inferred from the report's note).

timeline.event: Architect's post shows the complex after an earlier full remodel under the Adams County Housing Authority
Still listed on CHFA's Federal 4% award report (no 8609s yet)
